extracted.intended_audience: educators, students of education/philosophy, and policy-makers interested in vocational and democratic education
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guiding principles for designing and evaluating vocational education within a democratic philosophy of education, and for judging educational philosophies by their practical, educative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of vocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A vocation signifies any form of continuous activity which renders service to others and engages personal powers in behalf of the accomplishment of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this inclusive, service-and-engagement-based definition when identifying what counts as vocational work; emphasizes continuous activity and social usefulness rather than narrow technical tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct school materials and methods around occupations
rubrics_metrics.description: The key to the present educational situation lies in a gradual reconstruction of school materials and methods so as to utilize various forms of occupation typifying social callings, and to bring out their intellectual and moral content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and methods should connect classroom work with occupations, making learning active, meaningful, and tied to out-of-school experience; purely literary and dialectical methods (including textbooks) should be relegated to auxiliary roles rather than central ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid interpreting vocational education as mere trade education
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem is not that of making the schools an adjunct to manufacture and commerce, but of utilizing the factors of industry to make school life more active... There is a standing danger that vocational education will be interpreted in theory and practice as trade education: as a means of securing technical efficiency in specialized future pursuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not design vocational programs narrowly to reproduce current industrial practices or merely to train technical efficiency; beware that such narrow trade education will perpetuate existing industrial divisions and social predestination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include intellectual, historical, civic, and scientific dimensions in vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: An education which acknowledges the full intellectual and social meaning of a vocation would include instruction in the historic background of present conditions; training in science to give intelligence and initiative in dealing with material and agencies of production; and study of economics, civics, and politics...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocational programs should teach the scientific bases, historical context, and social/political dimensions of work, and should train adaptability so workers can respond to changing conditions rather than becoming appendages to machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use industry as an educative resource (shop and laboratory balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The laboratory has the advantage of permitting the following up of any intellectual interest a problem may suggest; the shop the advantage of emphasizing the social bearings of the scientific principle... Under the old regime all workers in a craft were approximately equals in their knowledge and outlook. Now the operator has to adjust himself to his machine...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning experiences that combine laboratory-style inquiry (to follow intellectual interests) with shop-based, socially-contextualized activities (to highlight social bearings), thus leveraging industry to foster insight rather than only mechanical skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocational education should develop intelligence and social control
rubrics_metrics.description: It would give those who engage in industrial callings desire and ability to share in social control, and ability to become masters of their industrial fate. It would enable them to saturate with meaning the technical and mechanical features which are so marked a feature of our machine system of production and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for vocational programs that cultivate initiative, critical understanding of work's social consequences, and capacities for participation in social decision-making—not merely technical competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose educational schemes that institutionalize class divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: To split the system, and give to others, less fortunately situated, an education conceived mainly as specific trade preparation, is to treat the schools as an agency for transferring the older division of labor and leisure, culture and service, mind and body, directed and directive class, into a society nominally democratic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether an educational design reinforces social stratification (liberal/cultural education for the privileged vs. narrow trade education for the masses); such stratifying schemes are condemned as perpetuating intellectual and moral dualisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as formation of fundamental dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: If we are willing to conceive education as the process of forming fundamental dispositions, intellectual and emotional, toward nature and fellow men, philosophy may even be defined as the general theory of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess educational aims by their capacity to form lasting intellectual and moral dispositions, not merely by transmission of facts; the success of a philosophy of education is measured in dispositional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophies must be connected to practice (practical test)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a theory makes no difference in educational endeavor, it must be artificial... Unless a philosophy is to remain symbolic... its auditing of past experience and its program of values must take effect in conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge educational philosophies by their practical consequences: do they produce educative changes in conduct, public action, or school practice? Theories disconnected from practice are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy distinct from science: focus on disposition toward action
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular facts and laws of science evidently influence conduct. When science denotes... a general attitude toward it--as distinct from special things to do--it merges into philosophy. Philosophy concerns the disposition toward the world which scientific disclosures exact of us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating educational aims, distinguish factual/scientific curriculum content from the broader philosophic dispositions schools should cultivate; avoid conflating empirical knowledge with philosophic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic disposition: totality as continuity and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Totality" means rather consistency of mode of response... Totality means continuity--the carrying on of a former habit of action with the readaptation necessary to keep it alive and growing... Any person who is open-minded and sensitive to new perceptions, and who has concentration and responsibility in connecting them has, in so far, a philosophic disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate persons' or programs' philosophic quality by continuity of response, openness, sensitivity, concentration, responsibility, and ability to learn from varied experiences rather than by rigid doctrinal completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as thinking about demands of the known (hypothetical, prospective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy is thinking what the known demands of us--what responsive attitude it exacts. It is an idea of what is possible, not a record of accomplished fact. Hence it is hypothetical, like all thinking. It presents an assignment of something to be done--something to be tried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use philosophy to frame problems, suggest methods, and assign practical experiments in education; emphasize that philosophies should be tested through action and remain open/hypothetical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy should integrate conflicting interests in society
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand for a 'total' attitude arises because there is the need of integration in action of the conflicting various interests in life... When the scientific interest conflicts with, say, the religious, or the economic with the scientific... there is a stimulus to discover some more comprehensive point of view from which the divergencies may be brought together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess educational philosophies by their capacity to reconcile or mediate conflicting social aims (scientific, religious, economic, aesthetic) and to recover continuity of experience at the community level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design education with awareness of social context and psychological development
rubrics_metrics.description: The advances which have been made in the psychology of learning... modern psychology emphasizes the radical importance of primitive unlearned instincts of exploring, experimentation, and 'trying on.'... the passage from play to work should be gradual, not involving a radical change of attitude but carrying into work the elements of play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocational and general curricula should incorporate psychological insights: provide gradual transitions from play to work, encourage exploration and experimentation, and structure occupations so learning organizes original capacities into meaningful activities.
